prompt.context: The year is 2013. Your client is a large New York based professional baseball team, the New York Shmankees. The owner, Baby Ruth, is by no means cheap and has a reputation for over-paying for some of the team's players. Baby Ruth has communicated to your firm that he has little desire to change that moving forward. However, there has been a decrease in the profit margins of the team over the last two regular seasons, and Baby Ruth has engaged your firm for help.
prompt.question: What key factors would you look at to address the decrease in profit margins?

clarifying_info.q: Does the client own any other teams or businesses?
clarifying_info.a: No, this is the only team Baby Ruth owns.

clarifying_info.q: What league does the team compete in?
clarifying_info.a: The Shmankees are a US-based professional baseball team out of New York City competing in the MLB as a member of the AL East Division. The team has been around since 1901 and has won 27 World Series Titles, more than any other team.

clarifying_info.q: How are other MLB teams doing?
clarifying_info.a: There are 30 MLB baseball teams and the profitability of the other teams has been mixed.

clarifying_info.q: What are the main revenue streams?
clarifying_info.a: Ticket Sales, Media Rights, Sponsorships, Memorabilia, and Concessions.
For simplicity, focus only on regular season profit margins and ignore post-season.
Return profit margin to the level it was in 2009.

exhibits.title: Shmankees Revenues and Costs Over Time
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis chart displaying the Shmankees' revenues and costs over multiple years (2009–2012). The left axis represents costs and the right axis represents revenues, both in millions of dollars.
exhibits.data: 2009: Revenue 400, Costs 360; 2010: Revenue 572, Costs 544; 2011: Revenue 628, Costs 597; 2012: Revenue 654, Costs 621

framework: Revenue: Ticket Sales (price per ticket, average attendance trends), Concessions (prices, items sold by product type and margin), Memorabilia (prices, items sold, impact of popular player departures), Media Rights (contract terms, % share, cord-cutting trends), Sponsorships

Costs — Fixed: Stadium (leased or owned), Player contracts (new high-salary signings, total payroll trends), Front office salaries; Costs — Variable: Hourly employees, Field maintenance, Player development, Technology, Travel (hotels, meals, airplanes)

Macro/External: Declining overall interest in sports/baseball, competition from streaming (Netflix etc.), team winning record, popularity of current player base, competition from other local sports teams or new entrants
Note: Given Baby Ruth's stated unwillingness to cut costs, the analysis should prioritize revenue growth opportunities over cost reduction

questions.prompt: Review Exhibit 1. What are your key takeaways, and what is the profit margin in 2009 versus 2012?
questions.guidance: Candidate should clarify that numbers are in millions and identify which axis is which. Strong candidates calculate profit margins for 2009 (target) and 2012 (current) and skip 2010/2011 as intermediate years. They should note that there are two levers — revenue increase or cost reduction — but then connect back to Baby Ruth's unwillingness to cut costs and focus on revenue. Best candidates proactively ask what analysis to do next.

math.setup: Profit = Revenue - Costs; Profit Margin = Profit / Revenue
math.answer: Current profit margin is approximately 5% (2012); target is 10% (2009 level). Revenue has grown but costs have grown proportionally faster, eroding margins.

questions.prompt: The team has determined they want to focus on increasing ticket prices. Current price is $30/ticket generating 2,762,100 tickets/yr. Option A: raise to $40 (2,511,000 tickets sold). Option B: raise to $50 (2,385,450 tickets sold). Projected other revenues for 2013 are $600mm; projected costs are $650mm. What is the optimal pricing strategy from a profit standpoint?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask for projected costs and recognize that tickets are only one revenue stream — they should ask about other revenues. Strong candidates note that a reduced fan base may negatively affect concessions, memorabilia, and other revenue streams. Candidate should round numbers to simplify math. The goal is to identify which price hits the 10% profit margin target.

math.setup: Total Revenue = Ticket Revenue + Other Revenue ($600mm). Profit = Total Revenue - Total Costs ($650mm). Profit Margin = Profit / Total Revenue.
math.answer: Raising ticket price to $50 achieves the target 10% profit margin. $40 only reaches ~7%. $30 status quo stays at ~5%.

brainstorming.prompt: Your team has gotten on the same page with Baby Ruth, and cost-cutting is out of the picture. Baby Ruth has asked you out to lunch at Joe's Pizza. Your manager has asked you to come up with additional revenue growth strategies to discuss over lunch. What would you plan to discuss?

categories.name: Game Day
ideas: Increase seating capacity (e.g., add standing-room sections)

categories.name: Non-Game Day / Off-Season
ideas: Memorabilia: increase prices, offer limited editions or player-specific items
Media Contracts: explore renegotiation opportunities to capture higher share
Marketing: player roadshows to build excitement, commercials, social media engagement
Expand fan base to new geographies (Japan, China) and underserved US markets

recommendation: Recommend that the Shmankees raise ticket prices to $50 per ticket for the 2013 season. At this price point and projected attendance of approximately 2,400,000 fans, combined with $600mm in other revenues and $650mm in costs, the team achieves a 10% profit margin — meeting Baby Ruth's objective of returning to 2009 levels.
risks: Long-term or price-sensitive fans may switch to other forms of entertainment
Fewer fans in the stadium may hurt atmosphere and player motivation
Negative PR perception of the team as unaffordable or elitist
Reduced attendance could have second-order negative effects on concession, memorabilia, and sponsorship revenues
next_steps: Stress-test assumptions: validate the attendance elasticity model at $50
Analyze other revenue streams (concessions, memorabilia, media rights) to identify further margin improvement opportunities
Monitor fan sentiment and attendance early in the season and adjust if needed
